title: [CI] GitHub CI at most 30 min per workflow; local act 16 CPUs per job, 4 jobs at once, signed 1-to-1 with GitHub CI; prebuilt tool layers
body:
## Why

A local act replay of a PR takes about 4.3 h, and GitHub CI takes up to 77 min. The owner, 2026-10-14 06:1x, said 4 hours is unacceptable. GitHub CI must finish in at most 30 min, and a local build must be provably 1-to-1 with what GitHub CI does, through some kind of signature. Local act jobs get 16 CPUs instead of 4, and the act may run 4 jobs at once. Prebuilt tool layers will come from a registry the owner is creating.

## Measured baseline

**GitHub CI, PR #736 head `7032bca5`, all four workflows started at the same time:**

| Workflow | Wall clock | Slowest jobs |
|---|---|---|
| rtl-full | 77 min | Verilator shards 2/5, 0/5, 1/5, 3/5, 4/5: 70, 69, 68, 60, 55 min |
| elaborate | 35 min | elaborate: 35 min |
| docs | 33 min | docs-check: 33 min |
| rtl-fast | 19 min | publication-census: 18 min; firmware-control-mutants: 16 min |

**Local act replay, #696 at `e2cd089c`: 4.27 h.**
- The four workflows run one after another: 29 + 33 + 99 + about 100 min.
- `scripts/act_ci.py` `CONCURRENT_JOB_LIMIT = 1`; only matrix legs overlap, at most 4.
- Each job sees 4 CPUs.
- Caches are ephemeral, so every run rebuilds Yosys (10 min) and Verilator (5 min) and reinstalls the other tools, about 21 min in total.
- The slot's memory peak was 18.3 GiB of its 24 GiB cap.

## Scope

1. **GitHub CI wall clock at most 30 min per workflow.**
   - Split the long jobs, starting with the Verilator suite, elaborate and docs-check, into more matrix legs.
   - Leg membership is derived from the suite's own inventory, never a hand list.
   - A final job proves the union of the legs equals the inventory: every test ran once, none missing or duplicated.
   - GitHub runners stay standard. Make no step conditional, drop no test, and raise no timeout to meet the target.
2. **Local act: 16 CPUs per job and up to 4 concurrent jobs.**
   - Each job container gets its own 16-CPU range.
   - `CONCURRENT_JOB_LIMIT` is 4, so independent jobs and workflows run side by side.
   - Size the slot memory cap from measured peaks; the host has 53 GB in total, shared with other work.
   - Keep the replay's verdict on the same head unchanged. This supersedes #730's `nproc = 4` fidelity item; `nproc` is now 16 per job.
3. **Prebuilt tool layers.**
   - Build Yosys, Verilator, the RV32 SDK, LiteX and the other tool installs as pinned image layers, keyed by exact version and source digest.
   - Pull them by digest from the owner's registry once it exists; the manager posts its address.
   - Until then, use a cache keyed the same way, so a changed pin always rebuilds.

4. **Signature: a local run is 1-to-1 with GitHub CI.**
   - A local act run emits a signed manifest that binds:
     - the exact head and tree;
     - the digests of the workflow files;
     - the job and step list actually executed, with each leg's inventory;
     - the container and tool-layer image digests;
     - the tool versions;
     - each job's result.
   - GitHub CI computes the same manifest over its own run, in the same canonical form, and a check compares the two.
   - Any difference in executed jobs, steps, inventories or images is refused by name.
   - Only a local run whose manifest equals GitHub CI's, apart from timing and runner identity, counts as equivalent.

## Acceptance

1. **GitHub CI:** on a PR that runs the full suite, every workflow's wall clock is at most 30 min, from the first job start to the last job end, with the union proofs passing.
2. **Local:** a full act replay of a known head reports the wall clock per workflow and per job, and the slot memory peak, before and after. It stays within the slot cap, with no OOM. Target: the same order as the hosted wall clock.
3. **Fidelity and signature:** the same head gets the same verdict locally and on GitHub CI, and the two manifests compare equal; a planted difference (a skipped step, a dropped test leg, a different image digest) is refused. Every planted defect a gate caught before is still caught.
4. **Docs:** `docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md` describes the sharding, the union proofs, the CPU and concurrency model, the tool-layer pinning and the signature.


## Plan details (owner-validated 2026-10-14 06:4x)

**Where the local 4.3 h goes** (#696 act `e2cd089c`, 15,360 s; #734 act `7c862ad9`, 4 h 13 min). The run holds 6.7 h of job time, run almost entirely in sequence:
- the four workflows replay one after another: docs 29 min, elaborate 33 min, rtl-fast 99 min of job time, rtl-full 243 min;
- `scripts/act_ci.py:119` `CONCURRENT_JOB_LIMIT = 1`, so only matrix legs overlap, at most 4;
- each job is held to 4 CPUs;
- caches are ephemeral, so every run rebuilds Yosys (10.2 min) and Verilator (5.0 min) and installs the rest, about 21 min in total.

**Owner answers:**
- An act replay gives each job 16 CPUs and runs **4 jobs at once**, 64 CPUs per replay.
- **No local registry mirror for now.** The slot data-roots already keep images (81 GB and 70 GB), so a new digest is pulled once per slot.

**Splitting `milan_dp`** (46.6 min of GitHub CI time). `tb/verilator/milan_dp/Makefile:545` (`run:`) runs the `gptp` and `gptp-lat` prerequisites, builds nine full Verilator binaries, runs each, then runs `counters`.
- Make one suite per leg, each building only its own binary plus the shared generated inputs (`ltn_rom.hex`, `ucode.hex`, `GEN_ALL`): 1x1 (`obj_dir`), nxn, nxndv, nxn8, nxn4c, nolpf, prune, ax1x1, aclk, gptp, gptp-lat, counters.
- Align the gptp leg with the existing `milan_dp_gptp` suite (5,400 s).
- Split `milan_dp_mclk` (34.0 min) the same way, and every other suite over about 15 min: `capture_coherence` 28.9, `maap` 22.9, `milan_dp_render` 21.1, `pp_shadow` 20.9.
- Register each leg in `scripts/run_all_suites.sh` (with `suite_timeout`) and in `scripts/suite_shards.py` `SUITE_SECONDS`, measured from one rtl-full run. Remove `milan_dp` from `DEDICATED_SUITES`.
- `suite_shards.py --selftest` keeps refusing missing durations and over-budget workers.

**Workers.** About 12 Verilator workers in `.github/workflows/rtl.yml`.
- Modelled longest shard: about 27 min, against 64 min today at 5 workers.
- With `milan_dp` unsplit, the longest shard stays at 46.6 min whatever the worker count.
- `tsn_fuzz` and `chmap_capture` are pinned to workers 1 and 3 only because those workers install extra tools. The image removes that need.

**Other long jobs.** Split `elaborate` (20.4 min of elaboration gates) and `docs-check` (16.1 min of builder gates) into parallel gate jobs, with the same union proof over the gates.

**Lanes:**
- `737-ci30`: executor A614, branch `737-ci-30min`. Sharding, act CPUs and concurrency, and the manifest base.
- `737-image`: executor A615, branch `737-ci-image`. The image recipe, lock file, tool inventory and `docs/testing/CI_IMAGE.md`.
- The signature design is in the [A10] comment of 2026-10-14 06:4x. It is committed as `docs/testing/CI_SIGNATURE.md`.

**Related:** #730 (act CPU ranges; its acceptance 4 is measured here), #734 (scope by merge base, merged as `fa7347fc`), #727 (shard balancing).


**Fail fast (owner, 2026-10-14 06:52).**
- The first failure stops the run: matrices use `fail-fast: true`, and the first failed job cancels its own run and the other workflows' runs at the same head SHA.
- A local act stops at the first failed job.
- Aggregates treat a cancelled leg as a failure, and a cancelled run is never a valid build. Details are in the [A10] fail-fast comment.


## Scope change (owner, 2026-10-14 12:5x)

The RTL workflows (`rtl.yml`, `rtl-fast.yml`) leave the PR and push triggers. The local act replay is the RTL build, and a PR gate on GitHub verifies its signed manifest. `rtl.yml` keeps its nightly run and `workflow_dispatch` as the fidelity check against GitHub's own run. Acceptance items 1 and 3 are replaced. Details: [6166823105](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/737#issuecomment-6166823105).
